newsitem.title: USA: Washington $425 mln stadium campaign gets underway.
newsitem.headline: Washington $425 mln stadium campaign gets underway.

text.p: Supporters of a proposed $425 million outdoor stadium for the Seattle Seahawks football team launched their campaign on Friday to sway skeptical Washington state voters to back the massive project.

Stadium supporters said they opened their campaign headquarters in Seattle along with field offices in Everett, Tacoma, Olympia, Vancouver, Tri-Cities-Yakima and Spokane. Other field offices will open in the coming weeks in Bellingham and Kitsap County, the campaign said.
"It's a fast campaign. We only have five weeks to go and we have a lot of people to organize," said Susan Oxholm, a spokeswoman for the stadium compaign.
Last month, Gov. Gary Locke signed a bill setting up a statewide vote on the financing package for the stadium. The package will be put to voters at a special election June 17.

Voters will be asked to approve new lottery scratch ticket games, to extend the existing hotel-motel tax in King County through the year 2020, to divert some sales tax revenue to the stadium, and to tax tickets and parking there. Those taxes raise should over $325 million over 20 years.

Prospective Seahawks buyer Paul Allen will chip in another $100 million to complete the package. The Microsoft Corp co-founder spent hundreds of thousands of dollars lobbying the state legislature and on television advertising to build public support.
